brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: 3-cell base (piece:0,0,0, 0,1,0, 1,0,0) forms compact tray with side walls capped; bins provide caddy function
Two hex-acc-handle accessories on opposite sides of central cell (accessory:0#0,0#1 and #4) give balanced carry grip

requirements.requirement: Divided bins for screws and bits
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0 hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) holds screws/nuts/standoffs per prop heap-screws-div3 etc; bins 0,1,0 and 1,0,0 hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments each) provide additional divided storage for screws/bits – total 7 compartments

finish.summary: Built L-shaped 3-cell caddy with three divided bins (3+2+2 compartments) and opposing grab handles on central cell. Props show screws/nuts/standoffs sorted. Open faces capped and joints locked, mesh clear.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Grab handle
parts.use: A bar standing off the flat with room for a hand behind it, for a cell or a column that gets moved by its side rather than its top.

parts.name: Trinity handle
parts.use: Reaches across a whole triangle of studs, so a lift is shared between recesses instead of hanging off one, and the cell can be carried loaded.
